stories.title: Sensex and Nifty climb as auto stocks rally
stories.summary: The Sensex rose 440 points and the Nifty gained 131 points on November 19, driven by a surge in auto stocks. Maruti Suzuki shares climbed 6.52 percent, while Eicher Motors and Tata Motors also saw gains. The market recovery followed an initial dip during the morning session.

stories.title: Auto stocks lead intraday market recovery
stories.summary: Benchmark indices recovered from early losses to trade higher on Thursday, with the Nifty up 138 points and the Sensex climbing 469 points. The rally was led by auto manufacturers including Maruti Suzuki and Eicher Motors. The indices had initially opened lower following hawkish US Federal Reserve minutes.

stories.title: Defence stocks rise on potential capital expenditure hike
stories.summary: Shares of defence companies including HAL, BEL and BDL rose up to 3 percent on Thursday. The gains followed government signals of a 20 percent hike in capital expenditure, potentially funding the acquisition of 114 Rafale fighter jets and six submarines. The sector remains focused on domestic procurement.

stories.title: Auto stocks rally as metal prices drop
stories.summary: The Nifty Auto index surged nearly 4 percent on Thursday as falling industrial metal prices eased input cost concerns. Maruti Suzuki led the gains with a 7 percent rise, while Hyundai, Eicher Motors and Mahindra and Mahindra also advanced. Copper and aluminium prices recently hit multi-month lows.

stories.title: BL Kashyap and Sons shares hit record high
stories.summary: Shares of B L Kashyap and Sons surged 15 percent on Thursday to reach an all-time high of 60.35 rupees. The move marked the company's largest single-day gain since April, with 48 million shares traded by noon. There was no immediate fundamental trigger for the sudden investor interest.

stories.title: Sensex and Nifty recover from early losses
stories.summary: Benchmark indices erased early declines to trade in the green on Thursday, supported by foreign fund inflows and lower crude oil prices. The Sensex rose 518 points despite a hawkish tone in recent US Federal Reserve minutes. The market turned positive after 10 am, led by large-cap stocks.

stories.title: PSU Bank index nears record high
stories.summary: The Nifty PSU Bank index rose 2.3 percent on Thursday, extending its monthly gains to over 18.5 percent. The rally was driven by Punjab National Bank, Bank of Baroda and State Bank of India. The index is currently approaching its February 2026 record high of 9,918.65.

stories.title: Sensex edges higher as auto sector leads
stories.summary: The Sensex closed 0.26 percent higher on Thursday, trading at 82,247.59. While 30 of 38 tracked sectors advanced, the index remains 4.78 percent below its 52-week high. The Sensex has gained 10.44 percent over the past three weeks, though its 50-day moving average remains below the 200-day average.

stories.title: Sensex closes higher as large-caps lead
stories.summary: The Sensex closed at 82,236.36, a 0.25 percent gain, as large-cap stocks offset sectoral headwinds. The index is currently 4.77 percent below its 52-week high. While the index trades above its 50-day moving average, the 50-day average remains below the 200-day average, suggesting a cautious medium-term outlook.

stories.title: Jio Financial and Bharat Forge report subsidiary investments
stories.summary: Jio Financial Services invested 123 crore rupees in its joint venture with BlackRock via a rights issue. Bharat Forge also invested 291 crore rupees in its subsidiary Kalyani Strategic Systems. Both companies maintained their existing equity structures through the transactions, using proceeds from recent capital placements.

stories.title: Sensex records modest gains
stories.summary: The Sensex closed 0.15 percent higher at 82,158.36 on Thursday. The index is 4.87 percent below its 52-week high but has gained 10.34 percent over the last three weeks. Despite short-term gains, the 50-day moving average remains below the 200-day average, indicating a continued consolidation phase for the market.

stories.title: Sensex and Nifty trade near session highs
stories.summary: The Sensex rose 530 points and the Nifty gained 161 points by Thursday afternoon, supported by bank and auto shares. The Nifty FMCG index also snapped a two-day losing streak. The broader midcap and smallcap markets followed the upward trend, rising 0.47 percent and 0.22 percent respectively.

stories.title: European stocks inch up as massive Anthropic IPO counters hawkish Fed - Investing.com
Anthropic prices IPO at 81 billion dollars
stories.summary: Shares in AI developer Anthropic are set to begin trading on Thursday. The company priced its initial public offering at 83 dollars per share, resulting in a 1.5 trillion dollar valuation. The listing follows a period of intense investor interest in the artificial intelligence sector.

stories.title: Asian markets rise following Anthropic IPO pricing
stories.summary: Asian equities and US stock futures rose on Thursday after Anthropic priced its IPO at 83 dollars per share, above its target range. The 81 billion dollar offering is the largest on record. The debut serves as a test for the AI trade, which has recently faced market pressure.

stories.title: Anthropic prices IPO above target range
stories.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at 83 dollars per share, exceeding its 70 to 78 dollar target. The offering, which includes 980 million shares, is one of the largest in history. The company is the first major frontier AI model developer to go public, testing investor appetite for the industry.

stories.title: Anthropic sets record for largest IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic confirmed an IPO price of 83 dollars per share, raising 81.3 billion dollars. The sale of 980 million shares surpasses SpaceX's 75 billion dollar record. The debut is considered a pivotal moment for the artificial intelligence boom, which has become a primary driver of recent stock market activity.

stories.title: US markets trade mixed ahead of Anthropic debut
stories.summary: US stock indexes ended mixed on Wednesday as investors weighed Nvidia earnings and hawkish Federal Reserve minutes. Trading remained choppy ahead of the Anthropic IPO pricing. While the Nasdaq closed slightly higher, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell, reflecting investor caution regarding the broader AI-driven market momentum.

stories.title: A fifth straight drop for the S&P 500 drags Wall Street to its longest losing streak since June - AP News
Wall Street ends mixed after Nvidia earnings
stories.summary: US stocks finished mixed on Wednesday as investors weighed Nvidia's quarterly results against hawkish Federal Reserve minutes. While the AI chipmaker beat analyst expectations and raised revenue forecasts, its shares fell 2.9 percent. The Dow ended lower, while the Nasdaq managed a modest gain.

stories.title: Wall Street prepares for Anthropic IPO frenzy, despite broader AI stock slump - Reuters
Asian markets decline as AI stocks swing
stories.summary: Asian shares mostly retreated Wednesday following losses in the AI sector on Wall Street. Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 0.6 percent, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng declined 0.4 percent. Japan also reported a 476.5 billion yen trade deficit for October, marking a 58 percent increase from last year.

stories.title: US tech stocks oscillate after Nvidia results
stories.summary: US tech stocks fluctuated following Nvidia's latest earnings report. The chipmaker raised its revenue forecast, with leadership describing the situation as business as usual despite a recent sell-off triggered by news of co-founder Jensen Huang's personal affairs.

stories.title: Anthropic IPO set to raise $90.4 billion
stories.summary: Anthropic is moving toward an IPO that could become the largest in history. The company expects to price shares above its initial $70 to $78 range. Including a $26 billion private placement, the offering is poised to raise approximately $90.4 billion for the AI firm.

stories.title: Sebi chairman rules out longer trading hours
stories.summary: Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey stated that extending market trading hours is not a priority for India. Pandey cited concerns regarding cybersecurity and potential pressure on market liquidity. The regulator previously returned proposals for longer derivatives trading hours, citing a need for thorough assessment.

stories.title: RBI tightens API security for financial institutions
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has directed banks and non-banking financial companies to strengthen digital security frameworks. The advisory focuses on API-based fund transfers and third-party system connections to mitigate rising cyberattack risks and unauthorized fund diversions. The regulator is now emphasizing stricter transaction monitoring.

stories.title: PNB shares rise despite RBI penalty
stories.summary: Punjab National Bank shares gained 3.6 percent on Wednesday after the lender disclosed a 1.24 lakh rupee penalty from the Reserve Bank of India. The fine was issued for non-compliance with operational guidelines regarding currency chests. The bank stated the financial impact is limited to the penalty.

stories.title: Court quashes prosecution sanction against Chanda Kochhar
stories.summary: The Bombay High Court quashed the prosecution sanction granted by ICICI Bank's board against former CEO Chanda Kochhar. The court ruled the board lacked the authority to grant such sanction under the Prevention of Corruption Act, noting that power rests exclusively with the Reserve Bank of India.

stories.title: Court clarifies authority in ICICI loan case
stories.summary: The Bombay High Court held that the Banking Regulation Act overrides the Companies Act regarding the removal of banking officers. The ruling quashed a prosecution sanction against former ICICI Bank CEO Chanda Kochhar, affirming that only the Reserve Bank of India holds the power to authorize such proceedings.

stories.title: Public sector banks report profit growth
stories.summary: India's public sector banks reported a combined net profit of 1.09 lakh crore rupees for the first half of the financial year, a 16.9 percent increase year-on-year. Total advances rose 18.8 percent to 136.4 lakh crore rupees, with MSME and agriculture lending showing significant growth.

stories.title: Sebi remains unpersuaded by extended trading hours
stories.summary: Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said extending stock market trading hours is not a priority for India. Pandey questioned whether longer sessions would improve efficiency, citing cybersecurity risks and potential liquidity pressure. The regulator is currently assessing the implications of longer sessions alongside global groups.

stories.title: Compliance deadlines approach for year-end
stories.summary: Companies face a series of tax and regulatory filings throughout November and December. Requirements include advance tax, annual ROC filings, and GST returns. Management is advised to prioritize early reconciliation and clear ownership to avoid late fees and governance issues as the year-end deadline approaches.

stories.title: FBR introduces identity-shielded appeals process
stories.summary: The FBR has launched an electronic, identity-shielded appeals system for sales tax and federal excise disputes. The agency has proposed a similar framework for income tax cases. Under the new rules, commissioners’ identities are concealed and hearings are conducted through secure digital channels.

stories.title: Wise CEO criticizes RBI payment cap
stories.summary: Wise CEO Kristo Käärmann questioned the Reserve Bank of India's 25 lakh rupee per-transaction cap on overseas payments for fintech companies. Käärmann argued the limit hinders Indian exporters. The cap applies to payment aggregator-cross border companies operating under direct supervision of the central bank.

stories.title: Sebi studies global stock lending models
stories.summary: Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the regulator is studying international stock lending and borrowing models to find a suitable system for India. Pandey reiterated that extending trading hours is not currently planned, citing increased risks and liquidity concerns as primary factors for the decision.

stories.title: Gold loan firms seek clarity on stressed assets
stories.summary: Gold loan firms are requesting RBI guidance on selling stressed loans to asset reconstruction companies. Industry officials suggest this route could help borrowers reclaim pledged jewellery, as current auction practices can permanently deprive households of assets following a 25 percent decline in gold prices over the year.

stories.title: Tiger-backed Razorpay nears IPO filing
stories.summary: Razorpay is preparing to file for an Indian IPO as early as next week, according to people familiar with the matter. The fintech firm is targeting a launch by February and could raise up to $600 million. The company is currently lining up its advisors.

UPI merchant fees may be capped at 5 rupees
stories.summary: Merchant-to-merchant payments on the UPI network are likely to carry a flat 5 rupee fee, according to reports. This rate is significantly lower than the 0.4 percent charge previously feared by traders. The National Payments Corporation of India has yet to set an official rollout date.

stories.title: Paytm shares fall on UPI fee delay
stories.summary: Shares of One 97 Communications dropped nearly 10 percent on Thursday following reports that the rollout of merchant transaction fees on UPI could be delayed again. The uncertainty has prompted concerns regarding the company's ability to generate additional revenue from its merchant payments business.

stories.title: UPI fee rollout may wait for 2027 elections
stories.summary: The introduction of merchant fees on UPI transactions could be delayed until after the 2027 state elections. Government officials are reportedly concerned about potential backlash from trade associations. Much of the regulatory and operational groundwork is complete, but an implementation date remains elusive.

stories.summary: Paytm shares came under sharp selling pressure on Thursday, November 19, falling nearly 7% as renewed concerns over a possible delay in implementing the proposed Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) framework for select Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions weighed on digital payments companies. stories.title: Payments stocks slide as UPI fee rollout stalls
stories.summary: Shares of Paytm, Pine Labs, and One Mobikwik Systems fell on Thursday following news that the implementation of UPI merchant fees remains postponed. The 0.4 percent fee announced in September was intended to end six years of free transactions. No new date has been set.

stories.summary: Reports suggest the implementation of MDR on select UPI transactions could be deferred until after assembly elections in five states during H1CY27, amid concerns over merchant opposition. stories.title: India REITs distribute 3,234 crore in second quarter
stories.summary: India's six publicly listed REITs distributed over 3,234 crore to more than 5.25 lakh unitholders during the second quarter. The Indian REITs Association stated that these trusts have cumulatively distributed over 38,000 crore since their inception, highlighting their growing role in the country's capital markets.

stories.title: Noida builder ordered to hand over flat
stories.summary: A consumer forum has ordered a builder to hand over a flat to a couple after the company failed to provide documents required for a home loan. The commission ruled that the lack of paperwork constituted a deficiency in service. The handover must occur within 30 days.

stories.title: Mutual funds take half of Mahanadi Coalfields anchor book
stories.summary: Domestic mutual funds secured 53 percent of the anchor allocation for the Mahanadi Coalfields IPO. The subsidiary of Coal India allocated 16.88 crore shares to anchor investors at 136 rupees each. The public subscription period for the offering runs from 19 November to 23 November 2026.

stories.title: Study suggests longer SIP horizons reduce risk
stories.summary: A 21-year study by Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund suggests that longer investment horizons in SIPs improve minimum returns and reduce the likelihood of negative outcomes. The analysis covered various market cycles, including the 2008 financial crisis and the COVID-19 period. Time is presented as a risk mitigation strategy.

stories.title: Kerala passes senior citizens protection bill
stories.summary: The Kerala Legislative Assembly unanimously passed the Keralam Senior Citizens Bill on 26 October. The state legislation aims to prevent financial exploitation, care-home pressure, and cyber fraud. It differs from the national MWPSC Act, which focuses on forcing children to pay maintenance or return gifted property. Prevention is now law.

stories.title: Gold prices hit 14-month low
stories.summary: Gold prices have fallen below $3,800 an ounce, while silver dropped to $45. A stronger US dollar, rising Treasury yields, and expectations of interest rate hikes have weighed on precious metals. Concerns over global economic growth have also pressured copper. Markets are currently reacting to the broader economic climate.

stories.title: Common reasons for 2026 income tax notices
stories.summary: Salaried employees may receive income tax notices despite filing returns and paying TDS. The Income Tax Department cites reasons including incorrect TDS deductions, inconsistencies between Form 16 and AIS, unreported income, and incorrect bank details. Filing a return does not necessarily mean the process is finished.

stories.title: Pensioners lobby 8th Pay Commission for higher payouts
stories.summary: The 8th Pay Commission, headed by Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai, is expected to submit its final report by mid-2027. Pensioners have used recent meetings in Bengaluru and Mumbai to reiterate their demand for 67 percent of their last basic pay as pension. The commission is currently hearing grievances.

stories.title: City Union Bank restricts gateway after unauthorised transaction
stories.summary: City Union Bank informed regulators of an unauthorised transaction involving its NEFT system on 16 November. The lender stated it took necessary steps to investigate the incident immediately. Shares of the bank were trading at 231.38 rupees following the disclosure. The bank says it followed all regulatory protocols.

stories.title: Borrowing against your Public Provident Fund
stories.summary: Public Provident Fund account holders can borrow up to 25 percent of their balance between the third and sixth financial years of opening an account. If the principal is repaid within 36 months, the interest rate is 1 percent. The facility is restricted to a specific window.

A blockchain may prove that a transaction satisfied. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
